reading.body:
CyrusOne Florence publishes 5 MW of IT capacity, making it the largest facility by disclosed specification in Kentucky, which holds three published capacity declarations totaling 9.55 MW across five mapped sites. The campus spans 143,000 square feet. At 40 kW per rack, this IT load is roughly 125 racks; at 300 kW per modern accelerator pod, it is roughly 17 pods.

The 5 MW figure is modest in the context of major AI scaling. It falls below the per-facility capacity of large cloud platforms and does not approach the single-site power budgets now consumed by frontier model training. Most data center capacity in Kentucky remains unpublished, so the state's true computational footprint is unknown. Whether additional capacity exists as dark inventory cannot be determined from public sources.

This site qualifies under PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and Green Globes certifications, indicating suitability for regulated workloads and security-conscious tenants. Whether it matters to AI depends on tenant workload and grid headroom that are not disclosed. The operator's site does not publish applied power draw, utilization rate, power purchase terms, or grid interconnection details. Without these facts, the facility's contribution to the AI compute supply chain cannot be assessed.
